mission: From the apartment, Ben and Talon watch news coverage frame Korda as the rogue center of the scandal. Aelia is pressured toward stepping down to preserve the Foundation. The public version of events is already calcifying — and it is incompatible with anything Ben could prove in the time remaining.
why_now: The public story is calcifying faster than the truth can catch it. Watching the news version of events cement Korda as a rogue bad actor and Aelia as a victim-reformer is a ticking clock: every hour the cover story hardens, it becomes more politically durable and legally harder to displace. Ben has to confirm, through this beat, that there is no version of the institutional path that arrives in time.
conflict: The cover story is professionally constructed and emotionally true in all the ways that matter to ordinary viewers. Aelia is being pressured toward stepping down to protect the Foundation's public mission — which is also something Ben can't dismiss, because the Foundation's public mission is real. The story is too neat, and Ben can see exactly why it works.
turning_point: Ben, Talon, and Luke (by holo) see the public story is too neat. The cover is moving faster than the truth.
closing_hook: Ben, Talon, and Luke (by holo) see the public story is too neat. The cover is moving faster than the truth.
setting: Coruscant, the Skywalker family apartment — daytime, kitchen and living area. Ben, Talon, and (by holo) Luke watch news coverage frame Korda as the rogue center of the scandal. The apartment is now their hideout; Talon has claimed the chair facing the door.

stakes.personal: Ben watches the public version of the last few weeks calcify into a story that makes the Vigil look like the victim of a rogue subordinate, Aelia look like a grieving reformer, and anyone who knows otherwise look paranoid or politically motivated. It’s the most dangerous thing Tess has done — not the violence, but the narrative.
stakes.interpersonal: Luke by holo: sees the cover moving faster than the truth. His response is careful and quiet — he doesn’t contradict the analysis, doesn’t offer false optimism. The call underlines what Ben already knows: there is no version of institutional action that arrives in the timeframe available.
stakes.external: The cover story is incompatible with anything Ben could prove in the time remaining. Every day it plays unchallenged it becomes more politically durable. The only counter is showing up on Iresh before the operation completes — so the event itself is the evidence, not the documentary reconstruction that was burned.

sensory_details: The apartment's daytime light comes at a low angle through the transparisteel — the same window that had rain on it during the first visit, now cold-gray and dry. Talon has claimed the chair facing the door; he never went back to the couch after the first night. The news display is projected from a small unit on the kitchen counter, the voice turned low enough that the presenter's inflection is clear but the actual words require attention. The news segment cuts to B-roll of the Foundation lobby — the scholarship walls Ben walked past, the engraved names from Fondor and Kuat and the refugee fleets. The coverage makes the Foundation's real grief into a backdrop for its own protection. Ben watches the wall he read in person become set-dressing for a story that is not true.
canon_elements_needed: Second Galactic Civil War and Yuuzhan Vong War dead on the Foundation's scholarship walls — the real grief the public story now weaponizes
The neat public story vs. the Foundation's actual work for named war-dead families: the cover is effective precisely because it borrows the Foundation's genuine credibility

turning_point_detail.trigger: Luke, watching the same coverage by holo, identifies the structural tell in the story: it resolves too cleanly and too quickly for an organization that large. The Korda fall-guy narrative answered every question before the questions were officially asked.
turning_point_detail.shift: Ben, Talon, and Luke all see it: the cover is moving faster than the truth. This is not sloppiness — it's preparation. Someone knew this moment would come and built a story for it in advance.
turning_point_detail.cost: The public version is already more politically durable than anything Ben could present to a magistrate. The only evidence that can override the narrative is stopping the Iresh operation in real time.

emotional_arc.start: Ben watches the news with the flat attention of someone reading for errors — looking for the seams in the cover story.
emotional_arc.shift: Luke's identification of the structural tell confirms what Ben already suspected: this was built, not improvised. The frustration is not at the story itself but at how good it is.
emotional_arc.end: The call ends. Ben and Talon have confirmed that there is no institutional path that arrives in time. They continue preparing for Iresh.

key_beats.beat_description: From the apartment, Ben and Talon watch news coverage frame Korda as the rogue center of the scandal — rogue security director, illegal contractors, no Foundation culpability.
key_beats.state_change: The public story is now running on its own momentum — every hour it plays unchallenged it becomes harder to displace.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Reading it the way you read a document for errors — the flat attention of someone looking for seams, not responding to content.

key_beats.beat_description: Coverage shows Aelia being pressured toward stepping down to protect the Foundation's charitable mission; the warmth shown her is genuine, which makes the story harder to attack.
key_beats.state_change: The cover story is emotionally true in all the ways that matter to ordinary viewers — it cannot be countered with the kind of evidence Ben no longer has.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The specific difficulty of watching Aelia's warmth confirm itself on screen — the recognition that she is not performing it for the cameras.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben identifies the structural tell in the cover: it resolves too cleanly and too quickly for an organization that size.
key_beats.state_change: The cover is confirmed as preparation rather than improvisation — someone built this story before they needed it.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The satisfaction of finding the seam immediately undercut by what the seam means — built-in-advance is worse than reactive.

key_beats.beat_description: Luke, watching the same coverage by holo, independently identifies the structural tell — the Korda narrative answered every question before the questions were officially asked.
key_beats.state_change: Ben's analysis is confirmed by Luke's read — the cover is built, not cobbled.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Luke seeing what he sees landing as both confirmation and a specific weight — the father seeing the same thing the son sees is not reassuring.

key_beats.beat_description: The call ends; Ben and Talon confirm there is no institutional path that arrives in the timeframe available — the only counter is showing up on Iresh before the operation completes.
key_beats.state_change: The analytical phase closes: the only evidence that can override the narrative is the operation itself, witnessed and stopped.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The decision already made registering as already-decided — not a new resolution, the recognition that it was never really a question.

Texture thread: The news B-roll cuts to the scholarship walls Ben walked past — Fondor, Kuat, the refugee-fleet columns, real engraved stone. The public story is borrowing the Foundation’s genuine grief as its credibility. Ben has the advantage of having read those names in person; he knows the difference between what the wall is and what the coverage is using it for. One beat, no editorial — the contrast speaks.
